responses.response: Keep the standard project config fields: schema, name, title, include.paths, and imageAliases. For shared specs, use a relative include such as ../shared inside include.paths. For shared images, keep the shared alias as @ pointing to ../shared/images/. The file must stay named likec4.config.json, all paths must be relative to projects/payments, and you should not use absolute paths, remove the @ alias, or replace working includes blindly.

Split it progressively, not all at once. Start with the minimal baseline: likec4.config.json, system-model.c4 for elements and relationships, and system-views.c4 for the index plus C1, C2, and C3 views. If dynamic flows become large, add a use-case or sequence file. If deployment detail becomes meaningful, add deployment files. If operations topology becomes meaningful, add operations files. View folders should be C1, C2, C3, Use Cases, Deployment, and Operations; only the index view stays at the root views block.

Edit the config surgically. Append the new shared source to include.paths instead of replacing existing entries, and keep all paths relative to the project folder. Preserve the existing config shape, especially schema, name, title, include.paths, and imageAliases. Keep the shared image alias working by leaving @ pointing to ../shared/images/ in place unless you are intentionally migrating icons. Avoid absolute paths, dropping aliases, or unrelated reorganization.

This skill is not enough by itself if you are adding a second LikeC4 project and deciding workspace-level structure. Use organize-multi-project for the multi-project boundary and workspace layout decisions, then use configure-project-includes for the new project local likec4.config.json, shared include paths, image aliases, and any small file split inside that project.

Append ../platform-shared after ../shared in include.paths, but keep the current shared image alias stable so existing icons still resolve. Keep @ pointing to ../shared/images/ and do not let the new source overwrite it. If you also need platform-specific images, add them under a separate non-colliding alias key instead of reusing @.

Use the smallest safe edit on the relevant sections and leave your existing schema, name, and title unchanged: include.paths should contain ../shared and ../platform-shared, and imageAliases should keep @ for ../shared/images/ plus a separate @platform alias for ../platform-shared/images/. This preserves current resolution while avoiding collisions.
